_about: Book and series descriptions for the public site. Edit here, not in the admin. Keys under "books" are the book ids from data.json.

The Marigold Brothers.tagline: Four brothers. One restaurant. The women who make them work for it.
The Marigold Brothers.setting: Sunday dinners and second chances · Marigold, Georgia
The Marigold Brothers.intro: The Calogeras brothers feed the whole town of Marigold, Georgia, but none of them knows how to let anybody feed them back. Four standalone sweet romances about kitchens, grief, family and the women who turn the quietest rooms in the house back into the loudest.

The Tolliver Swifts.tagline: A baseball family with four sons, four games to win, and hearts that don't know when to quit.
The Tolliver Swifts.setting: Ballpark lights and front porches · Tolliver, Alabama
The Tolliver Swifts.intro: In Tolliver, Alabama, the ballpark came before the town. Four sweet small-town romances set around Solomon Field and the Tolliver Swifts, about family legacy, holding on to what's yours and finally letting someone in.

The Men of Cauble Holler.tagline: Down in the holler, loyalty runs deep and love runs deeper.
The Men of Cauble Holler.intro: Up a mountain where everybody knows everybody, the men of Cauble Holler hold the place together with their own two hands. Sweet small-town romance about loyalty, patience and the people worth crossing the room for.

rdw-save-room.description:
He hasn't set foot in a kitchen in three years. She's about to turn the quietest room in the house back into the loudest.
In Marigold, Georgia, Sunday dinner is sacred. Chef Novalee Rhone is just there to cook it.
After losing her Atlanta restaurant, and most of herself with it, Novalee takes a standing job making Sunday dinner for the big, loud Calogeras family. It's supposed to be rent money. It's not supposed to be the eldest son.
Theron Calogeras hasn't crossed a kitchen threshold since his wife died. He stands in the doorway instead, every Sunday, watching a woman bring a room back to life. Soon he's showing up two hours early to fix hinges that aren't broken. She knows the hinges aren't broken. Neither of them says why.

rdw-made-from-scratch.description:
Evander Calogeras is the man who feeds Marigold, Georgia. The famous olive loaf, the free day-old shelf, the funeral bread nobody's ever been charged for. Everybody loves the baker. Nobody knows he's been quietly bleeding his own savings dry to keep his mama's hundred-year-old bakery alive, because asking for help is the one recipe he never learned.
Then he misses a loan covenant, and the bank sends Octavia Reese.

rdw-come-hungry.description:
He's the fastest man in Georgia at leaving. She's the most rooted woman in town. They've got twelve weeks.
Dimos Calogeras can charm a whole county and has never once stayed for the thank-you. Traveling physical therapist, favorite uncle, always packed, always gone before anyone gets close enough to need him. It's a good life, right up until his mother's knee surgery hands him a twelve-week contract in the one town he can't drive away from.
Zora Bell has done every head in Marigold for nine years. She runs the only Black-owned salon in three counties, keeps the whole town's secrets, and holds a standing offer from an Atlanta studio she's never let herself say yes to, because everybody here needs her, and being needed is the only kind of love she trusts.

rdw-second-helpings.description:
He cooks his grandmother's food so he never has to make his own. She arranges everyone's flowers and keeps none for herself. Two people who carry grief walk into the same small town.
Anatole Calogeras is the youngest Calogeras, the family's easy smile, and the one nobody can reach. Ten years ago the grandmother who raised him at her stove died, and he came home and never cooked his own food again, only hers, in someone else's kitchen, like penance. Everyone thinks he's healing. He's just gotten better at hiding the door.
Selene Okonkwo moved two hundred miles to open a flower shop where nobody knew to be careful with her. She lost her sister and business partner in the same afternoon, and now she translates every griever in town into stems and hands them back wrapped, while her own shop stays bare.

rdw-the-long-game.description:
She's never asked anybody for anything. He's never stayed anywhere past September.
In Tolliver, Alabama, the ballpark came before the town. Dinah Tolliver's great-great-granddaddy bought the ground seven years out of bondage, her grandfather built Solomon Field on it and hung the lights, and now the Tolliver Swifts are hers: a fifth-place club, a father recovering up on the hill, and a debt coming due that could take all of it. Nobody knows. Nobody's going to know. A Tolliver holds.

rdw-caught-looking.description:
She's spent eleven years on the radio in her father's voice. He's the first person to hear hers.
In Tolliver, Alabama, Marva Sloane is the voice of the Swifts. Eleven years in the booth, four counties listening, and every word of it belongs to her late father. She took the microphone the week they buried him and hasn't missed a broadcast since, and the whole town loves her for how much she sounds like Lou. Nobody has ever heard what Marva sounds like when she isn't being him. Least of all Marva.

rdw-home-field.description:
She's spent her whole life guarding one patch of ground so nobody can take it. He's a Lambert, and taking ground is the only thing his family was ever good at.
Clem Mosely has tended the field at Solomon Field for twenty years, and she keeps it the way she keeps everything: alone, perfect, and fenced. Her people worked land they were never allowed to own, and got moved off it, generation after generation, and Clem learned the lesson in her bones. The only ground you keep is the ground you hold with both hands. She hands nobody her tools. She bungees the gate herself every morning. And she has spent her whole life making sure nothing can ever be taken from her again.

rdw-safe-at-home.description:
She takes every picture in this town. She's in none of them.
For six seasons, Lena Ruiz has been the eye of Tolliver, Alabama. Twelve hundred photographs on the ballpark wall, every face this town loves, every moment that ever mattered. And if you walked that wall end to end, you would not find one single picture of the woman who took them all.
That is not an accident. It is the most deliberate thing she has ever made.
Then a sports photographer drives into town to shoot the Swifts' pennant run, and Sawyer Vance does the one thing nobody in six years has managed. He raises his camera at her.

rdw-hold-the-line.description:
For three years, the sheriff of Cauble Holler has sat two booths away every Thursday night, close enough to listen, too careful to cross the room.
Summer Wallace left a big-city firm to do small, honest law up a mountain, one free hour a week in the diner for the folks who can't pay for a lawyer and are scared of what the mail sent them. She reads documents because paper only ever says what it says. People are the ones who lie.
Sheriff Wyatt Yancey reads people the way Summer reads a deed, down to the bone, everybody in the county but himself. Divorced, gray at the temples, holding a whole holler together with his two hands and letting nobody carry any of it with him. For three years, neither of them has closed the distance.
